name: Philosophical Challenges of Artificial Minds
description: The rapid development of artificial intelligence and its increasing integration into everyday life have transformed the classical philosophical question of whether machines can think into something more urgent and complex. What kind of minds do artificial systems have, and what does the answer imply for our understanding of knowledge, agency, and responsibility? How we assess the capacities and limits of artificial minds shapes how we interpret what they produce, how we assign responsibility when their actions cause harm, and how we think about aligning machine behaviour with human interests. This course examines these questions as philosophical problems that matter for how we live, work, and make decisions alongside artificial minds.
